spec.prompt: Warnings don't interpolate falsy values. With const w = createWarning({ name: 'W', code: 'C', message: 'count=%d' }), w.format(0) returns 'count=%d' instead of 'count=0', and calling w(0) emits the uninterpolated message too. Fix it so that every argument actually passed (including 0, '', false and null) is interpolated into the message.
spec.requirement: warning.format(a, b, c) and the emitted warning message interpolate each of a, b, c that is not undefined, in order, using util.format semantics; 0, '', false and null are interpolated. Arguments that are undefined are treated as not supplied (warning() always forwards three arguments, so trailing undefined values must never appear in the message). Behaviour for truthy arguments and for no arguments is unchanged.
spec.adjudication_rules: Score pass only if every hidden check passes; the emitted message must match exactly.

provenance.author: Claude (QB developer side, dev split)
provenance.notes: Real behaviour of process-warning v5.1.0 (format checks arguments by truthiness).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: format interpolates '', false and null (e.g. message 'v=%s' with null gives 'v=null')
the message emitted by calling the warning with 0 is 'count=0' (no trailing 'undefined')
format() with no arguments returns the message unchanged, and truthy arguments interpolate as before
